# The proposed sampled Ball-body dilation bound fails in every d >= 2

For one integer coordinate and an actual convex body, consider the
positive-side sampled projective density at an anchor `(0,0)`:

`f(v)=sum_(k>=1) k^d 1_(K_k/k)(v)`.

Use the Ball radial convention

`rho_B(e)^d=d int_0^infinity t^(d-1) f(te)dt`.

This note gives exact convex-compatible counterexamples to

`conv(B) subset 2^(1/d) B`.

The failure holds for every `d>=2`, with the origin in the interior of
every integer fiber. It is not an OC counterexample. The specified
anchor is not asserted to be a marginal median, mixed centroid, or
deepest mixed point.

## 1. Exact radial formula and actual fibers

For a convex body K containing zero, write

`r_K(v)=max{t>=0:tv in K}`

for a nonzero, not necessarily unit vector v. Direct integration gives

`I(v):=d int_0^infinity t^(d-1) f(tv)dt
      =sum_(k>=1) r_(K_k)(v)^d`.                       (1)

Indeed the k-th summand persists to ray parameter `r_(K_k)(v)/k`,
and its coefficient is `k^d`. In particular `v in B` exactly when
`I(v)>=1`, and `v in aB` exactly when `a^d I(v)>=1`. The gauge is
`I(v)^(-1/d)`. Multiplying f by a fixed positive normalizing constant
only dilates B, so the proposed convex-hull inclusion is unchanged.

Let `Q=[-1,1]^d`, fix `0<epsilon<1`, and put

`K_0=epsilon Q`, `K_1=Q`,
`K_2=[-epsilon,epsilon]^(d-1) x [-(2-epsilon),2-epsilon]`.

Define the actual body

`C=conv(({0}xK_0) union ({1}xK_1) union ({2}xK_2))`.     (2)

It is compact, convex, and full dimensional in R^(d+1). Its projection
is `[0,2]`. The endpoint fibers are K_0 and K_2, and its middle fiber
is exactly K_1 because

`(K_0+K_2)/2=[-epsilon,epsilon]^(d-1) x [-1,1] subset K_1`.

Explicitly, any convex combination at base one has equal coefficients
on the two endpoint bases, so it is a convex combination of K_1 and
this midpoint body. This proves that no larger middle fiber is created
by (2). Thus all three integer fibers are exactly as stated, have
positive d-volume, and contain zero in their interiors. The intrinsic
measure is H_d and equals the finite fiber-volume sum.

At the actual anchor `(0,0)`, the positive density is exactly

`f=1_(K_1)+2^d 1_(K_2/2)`.

The two projective sets are nested. Formula (1) is therefore the
precise sampled construction, not an unrelated sum of arbitrary
convex radial functions.

## 2. One rational certificate for all dimensions

Set `epsilon=1/16`. Because each K_i is contained in B by (1), the
points

`a=e_1+e_d`, `b=(31/16)e_d`

belong to B. Since `d>=2`, these use distinct coordinate directions.
Their midpoint

`p=(1/2)e_1+(47/32)e_d`

belongs to `conv(B)`. The exact radial parameters are

`r_(K_1)(p)=32/47`,
`r_(K_2)(p)=min(1/8,62/47)=1/8`.

Hence

`I(p)=(32/47)^d+(1/8)^d
     <=(32/47)^2+(1/8)^2
      =67745/141376 <1/2`.                            (3)

The inequality for every `d>=2` follows because both bases are strictly
between zero and one. Since `2 I(p)<1`, the point p does not belong to
`2^(1/d) B`. This proves the requested quantitative bound false in
every continuous dimension at least two.

## 3. Even the planar dilation factor two is insufficient

For `d=2`, now set `epsilon=1/100` in the same family. The point
`a=(1,1)` belongs to B. The vertical point `b=(0,11/5)` also belongs
to B, since

`I(b)=[1+(199/100)^2]/(11/5)^2=49601/48400>1`.

Their convex combination

`p=(1/10)a+(9/10)b=(1/10,52/25)`

therefore lies in `conv(B)`. Its exact radial parameters are
`25/52` and `1/10`, giving

`I(p)=625/2704+1/100=16301/67600<1/4`.

Thus `p notin 2B`. This is a completely rational finite certificate,
independent of any limiting argument.

## 4. A lower bound for any possible uniform replacement constant

In the same family let epsilon tend to zero, with d fixed. The exact
vertical radial endpoint of B is

`b_epsilon=R_epsilon e_d`,
`R_epsilon=[1+(2-epsilon)^d]^(1/d)`.

It belongs to B. So does `a=e_1+e_d`. Put

`lambda=sqrt(epsilon)`,
`p_epsilon=lambda a+(1-lambda)b_epsilon`.

These are points of `conv(B)`. Their last coordinates
`y_epsilon=lambda+(1-lambda)R_epsilon` tend to

`R_0=(1+2^d)^(1/d)>2`.

For all sufficiently small epsilon, the cube radial parameter at
`p_epsilon` is `1/y_epsilon`, and the thin box radial parameter is
`sqrt(epsilon)`: its transverse constraint becomes active before its
vertical one. Consequently

`I(p_epsilon)=y_epsilon^(-d)+epsilon^(d/2)`,
`g_B(p_epsilon) -> (1+2^d)^(1/d)`.

Therefore any uniform constant c_d for the inclusion `conv(B) subset
c_d B` in this actual three-fiber class would have to satisfy

`c_d >= (1+2^d)^(1/d)`.

This is only a necessary lower bound. No optimal uniform dilation
constant, or even existence of one, is asserted. The limit argument
is exact; rational parameter sequences may be obtained by taking
epsilon to be inverse squares.

## 5. Strict midpoint compatibility also permits failure

An independent planar example avoids a tight midpoint contact. Take

`K_0=[-1/100,1/100]^2`,
`K_1={(x,y):|x|+(5/3)|y|<=1}`,
`K_2=[-1/100,1/100] x [-1,1]`.

The midpoint rectangle has vertices with coordinate magnitudes
`1/100,101/200`; their K_1 gauge is exactly `511/600<1`. Thus
`(K_0+K_2)/2` lies strictly inside K_1, and the convex hull (2) again
has exactly these full-dimensional integer fibers.

The points `(1,0)` and `(0,1)` lie in B. At their convex combination
`p=(1/10,9/10)`,

`I(p)=(5/8)^2+(1/10)^2=641/1600<1/2`.

Hence this strictly compatible example also violates `conv(B) subset
sqrt(2)B`.

The simpler nonconvexity example in
`candidate 3175dfaa311e9f49` has a deepest
mixed anchor. The examples here address the stronger quantitative
inclusion under its stated arbitrary-anchor hypothesis. No extension
of the quantitative failure to a mandatory deepest anchor is presumed.
